subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: At which historic session in 1955 did the Indian National Congress formally pass a resolution declaring a 'Socialistic Pattern of Society' as the goal of Indian planning?
options: A) Avadi Session (near Madras)
B) Nagpur Session
C) Calcutta Session
D) Belgaum Session
questions.explanation: At the 60th annual session of the Congress held in Avadi (Tamil Nadu) in January 1955 under U.N. Dhebar's presidency, the party adopted the 'Socialistic Pattern of Society' resolution.

questions.question: Which historic pact was concluded in July 1952 between Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir Sheikh Abdullah outlining the constitutional relationship between the state and the Union?
options: A) Srinagar Protocol of 1950
B) Delhi Agreement of 1952
C) Jammu Concordat of 1954
D) Lahore Declaration of 1951
questions.explanation: The 1952 Delhi Agreement settled key issues between New Delhi and Srinagar, accepting the extension of Indian citizenship, fundamental rights, and supreme court jurisdiction to J&K with state autonomy.

questions.question: Who was the legendary Gujarati cooperative pioneer who partnered with Tribhuvandas Patel and Dr. Verghese Kurien to build the Kaira District Milk Producers' Cooperative (Amul)?
options: A) C. Subramaniam
B) K. Kamaraj
C) H.M. Dalaya
D) Morarji Desai
questions.explanation: H.M. Dalaya, a dairy technologist, invented the groundbreaking process of making skimmed milk powder from buffalo milk, enabling Amul's revolutionary dairy expansion.

questions.question: On which day did Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri tragically pass away in Tashkent, hours after signing the peace agreement with Pakistani President Ayub Khan?
options: A) 10 January 1966
B) 15 August 1965
C) 26 January 1966
D) 11 January 1966
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died suddenly of a heart attack in Tashkent, USSR, in the early hours of 11 January 1966, shortly after signing the Tashkent Declaration.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which Burmese diplomat and educator served as the third Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1961 to 1971, facilitating mediation during the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis?
options: A) U Thant
B) Trygve Lie
C) Dag Hammarskjold
D) Kurt Waldheim
questions.explanation: U Thant of Burma (now Myanmar) served two terms as UN Secretary-General between 1961 and 1971, playing a vital role in defusing the Cuban Missile Crisis and resolving the 1965 India-Pakistan war.

questions.question: What radical political concept did socialist thinker Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia propound under the philosophy of 'Chaukhamba Raj' (Four-Pillar State)?
options: A) A four-member presidential executive ruling India through military decrees
B) Decentralization of political and economic sovereignty equally across four tiers: Village, District, Province, and Centre
C) The partitioning of the Indian subcontinent into four linguistic zones governed by the United Nations
D) A four-stage economic development plan funded entirely by foreign corporate capital
questions.explanation: Lohia propounded 'Chaukhamba Raj' as a model of radical socialist decentralization, distributing sovereign state authority across four democratic tiers: village, district, province, and centre.

questions.question: What was the core constitutional controversy surrounding the Merger Agreement signed by Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh of Manipur in September 1949?
options: A) The agreement was nullified by the International Court of Justice for violating the United Nations Charter
B) The Maharaja demanded that Manipur be granted complete sovereignty over the neighboring state of Assam
C) The Maharaja was pressured into signing the merger without consulting Manipur's popularly elected Legislative Assembly, creating long-lasting regional resentment
D) The agreement compelled all residents of Manipur to adopt Hindi as their exclusive mother tongue
questions.explanation: The Government of India succeeded in pressuring the Maharaja into signing the Merger Agreement in September 1949 without consulting Manipur's elected assembly, breeding enduring political alienation.

questions.question: Why did the land reforms legislation relating to the ceiling on agricultural land holdings largely fail across Indian states in the 1950s and 1960s?
options: A) The Supreme Court declared all state land reform acts unconstitutional and restored the British zamindari system
B) The Union Government lacked the constitutional power under the Seventh Schedule to pass agricultural laws
C) Rural landless laborers violently refused to accept redistributed agricultural plots
D) Landowners took advantage of numerous legal loopholes, delayed litigation in courts, and transferred surplus land to relatives (benami transfers)
questions.explanation: Land ceiling laws were undermined by feudal landlord evasion, fictitious transfers (benami transactions), judicial delays, and lack of political will among state-level ruling elites.

questions.question: What was the domestic political fallout of the 1962 Sino-Indian War on the Communist Party of India (CPI)?
options: A) It widened ideological fractures within the CPI between the pro-Soviet leadership supporting Nehru and the pro-Beijing/dissenting faction that formed the CPI(M) in 1964
B) It forced the CPI to dissolve its cadre and merge unconditionally with the Bharatiya Jana Sangh
C) It led to a nationwide constitutional ban prohibiting communist candidates from contesting parliamentary elections
D) It caused the CPI to align with the Swatantra Party to demand alignment with Western military pacts
questions.explanation: The 1962 war intensified the schism in the CPI: the dominant faction backed Nehru's government while dissidents (opposed to Moscow's revisionism) faced state arrests, culminating in the 1964 split.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: What institutional mechanism did the Samyukta Vidhayak Dal (SVD) coalition governments form in 1967 adopt to manage policy friction among ideologically conflicting member parties?
options: A) A joint military supervisory council composed of state police inspectors
B) A 'Common Minimum Programme' (CMP) agreed upon by all coalition partners
C) A rotating Chief Minister system where ministers changed every 15 days
D) A referendum conducted among the electorate on every disputed legislative bill
questions.explanation: SVD ministries formed in 1967 pioneered the adoption of a Common Minimum Programme (CMP) to bridge the ideological gulf between disparate constituents like the socialists, Jana Sangh, and BKD.

questions.question: What was the significance of the 20-Point Programme announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on 1 July 1975, immediately following the declaration of Emergency?
options: A) It was a military roadmap outlining the planned nuclear bombardment of neighboring hostile countries
B) It was a judicial manifesto dissolving all High Courts and establishing state-run military tribunals

C) It was a package of socio-economic measures including land distribution, liquidation of rural debts, worker participation in management, and anti-smuggling drives to project a progressive face for the regime
D) It was a foreign investment charter inviting American and British multinational corporations to manage public railways
questions.explanation: The 20-Point Programme sought to build popular legitimacy for the Emergency regime by highlighting rapid economic delivery, inflation control, land redistribution, and rural debt relief.

questions.question: Which crucial amendment did the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, introduce into Article 352 regarding the proclamation of Emergency on internal grounds?
options: A) It prohibited the President from ever proclaiming an emergency under any circumstance whatsoever
B) It required that an emergency must be ratified by a referendum of all registered voters
C) It transferred the emergency proclamation authority from the President to the Chief Justice of India
D) It replaced the ambiguous phrase 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'
questions.explanation: To prevent future executive misuse of Article 352, the 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion', ensuring an emergency cannot be declared to quell peaceful political protests.

questions.question: What triggered the eruption of armed separatist militancy in the Kashmir Valley in late 1989 and early 1990?
options: A) Widespread popular outrage over the alleged rigging of the 1987 state assembly elections, which delegitimized democratic politics and led disaffected youth to take up arms
B) The signing of a bilateral trade pact between India and Pakistan in Srinagar
C) The abolition of state foodgrain subsidies by the central planning commission
D) The construction of a multi-lane highway linking Jammu with New Delhi
questions.explanation: The blatant rigging of the 1987 elections in favor of the NC-Congress alliance against the Muslim United Front (MUF) destroyed youth faith in electoral democracy, sparking armed insurgency.

questions.question: What was the political ideology of the 'Bahujan' conceptualized by Kanshi Ram and mobilized by the Bahujan Samaj Party?
options: A) Forming a pan-Indian trade union exclusively of heavy industrial factory workers
B) Uniting the 85% majority consisting of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and religious minorities to challenge upper-caste hegemony
C) Organizing rural peasant landlords to demand complete exemption from income taxation
D) Promoting Vedic Sanskrit education across public universities in northern India
questions.explanation: Kanshi Ram defined the 'Bahujan' as the 85% demographic majority (SC, ST, OBC, minorities) that remained politically disenfranchised by the 15% upper-caste ruling elite.

questions.question: In the general elections of 2004, which historic coalition government assumed power at the Centre with Dr. Manmohan Singh as Prime Minister?
options: A) National Democratic Alliance (NDA)
B) United Front (UF)
C) United Progressive Alliance (UPA)
D) National Front (NF)
questions.explanation: The Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) came to power in May 2004 with outside support from the Left parties, and Dr. Manmohan Singh was appointed Prime Minister.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What was the fate of the extensive social welfare system of the Soviet Union (free healthcare, subsidized housing, guaranteed employment) following the collapse in 1991?
options: A) It was expanded across Western Europe through a series of bilateral trade agreements
B) It was placed under the permanent administration and funding of the United Nations Security Council
C) It was converted into a gold-backed private dividend fund paying annual royalties to every Russian citizen
D) It was largely dismantled under free-market Shock Therapy, pushing millions of vulnerable citizens and pensioners into sudden poverty
questions.explanation: Shock Therapy abruptly terminated state subsidies, demolished welfare nets, wiped out savings through inflation, and impoverished vulnerable populations and retirees across post-Soviet Eurasia.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the primary function of the European Court of Justice (ECJ) seated in Luxembourg?
options: A) Ensuring that EU law is interpreted and applied consistently across all member states and ruling on disputes involving EU institutions and governments
B) Conducting criminal trials for international war crimes committed during colonial wars
C) Setting interest rates and printing banknotes for the European Central Bank in Frankfurt
D) Inspecting military nuclear warheads deployed by NATO across the European continent
questions.explanation: The ECJ is the supreme judicial authority of the European Union, ensuring that EU treaties and regulations are interpreted and enforced uniformly across member states.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: In which Chinese city did the tragic military crackdown on pro-democracy student protesters take place in Tiananmen Square in June 1989?
options: A) Shanghai
B) Beijing
C) Guangzhou
D) Nanjing
questions.explanation: In June 1989, Chinese authorities used tanks and troops to crush massive pro-democracy demonstrations led by students in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, killing hundreds.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In Nepal, which comprehensive peace agreement signed in November 2006 formally concluded the decade-long civil war between the government and the Maoist rebels?
options: A) Kathmandu Protocol
B) Seven Party Concordat
C) Comprehensive Peace Accord (CPA)
D) Lumbini Declaration
questions.explanation: The Comprehensive Peace Accord (CPA) was signed on 21 November 2006 between Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala and Maoist chief Prachanda, ending the armed conflict and bringing Maoists into mainstream politics.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the unique voting feature of the 'Group of Four' (G4) nations—India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan—in their campaign for UN Security Council reform?
options: A) They have collectively withdrawn their ambassadors from the United Nations General Assembly
B) They hold a joint revolving seat on the International Court of Justice in The Hague
C) They have pledged never to maintain standing conventional armed forces
D) They mutually support each other's bids for permanent seats on an expanded UN Security Council
questions.explanation: The G4 countries (India, Brazil, Germany, and Japan) form an alliance supporting each other's bids for permanent seats on an enlarged UN Security Council.

questions.question: What is the strategic objective of 'Balance of Power' in classical international security?
options: A) Preventing any single state from becoming disproportionately powerful and dominant through internal armament and diplomatic alliance-building
B) Distributing all global industrial wealth equally among all sovereign governments
C) Requiring all national parliaments to pass identical military defense spending bills
D) Conducting annual nuclear weapon audits supervised by private multinational banks
questions.explanation: Balance of power is an equilibrium strategy where states build their own capabilities and forge alliances to deter any single power from achieving hegemony and dictating terms.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In which landmark environmental publication of 1962 did American marine biologist Rachel Carson expose the ecological hazards of synthetic chemical pesticides like DDT?
options: A) The Limits to Growth
B) Silent Spring
C) Our Common Future
D) Small is Beautiful
questions.explanation: Rachel Carson's 'Silent Spring' (1962) documented the devastating impact of indiscriminate pesticide spraying on birds, ecosystems, and human health, launching the modern environmental movement.

questions.question: What is the economic phenomenon of 'Brain Drain' frequently debated in the context of globalization in developing countries?
options: A) The loss of intellectual memory caused by widespread exposure to Western electronic entertainment
B) The complete shutdown of state universities in developing countries due to budget deficits
C) The emigration of highly skilled professionals, scientists, and doctors from developing nations to developed economies offering higher remuneration
D) The mandatory relocation of computer programmers to rural agricultural communes
questions.explanation: Brain drain refers to the large-scale migration of educated, talented professionals from developing countries (like India) to Western nations, depriving their home country of critical human capital.

questions.question: What was the main purpose behind the enactment of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act in 1969?
options: A) To compel all private companies to sell their shares exclusively to foreign multinational banks
B) To eliminate the state public sector from heavy capital goods manufacturing
C) To mandate that all private manufacturing plants must be located within port cities
D) To prevent the concentration of economic power in the hands of a few industrial conglomerates and control restrictive trade practices
questions.explanation: Enacted in 1969 under Indira Gandhi, the MRTP Act aimed to curb monopolistic concentration of private economic wealth and prohibit restrictive and unfair trade practices.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following describes the key achievement of the 1994 Marrakesh Agreement signed in Morocco?
options: A) Concluding the Uruguay Round of multilateral trade negotiations and formally creating the World Trade Organization (WTO)
B) Establishing the African Union with a common currency and continental central bank
C) Partitioning international airspace among the permanent members of the UN Security Council
D) Banning all fossil fuel exploration in developing nations by multinational oil firms
questions.explanation: Signed on 15 April 1994 by 123 nations, the Marrakesh Agreement concluded the 8-year Uruguay Round of GATT negotiations and established the WTO on 1 January 1995.

questions.question: Which landmark resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru at the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress in 1931 first articulated the commitment to Fundamental Rights and a National Economic Programme?
options: A) Poona Pact on Communal Representation
B) Resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Programme
C) Bombay Plan for Industrialization
D) Delhi Declaration on Provincial Autonomy
questions.explanation: Drafted by Nehru and Patel at Karachi in 1931, the resolution committed the Congress to basic civil liberties, adult franchise, labor protections, and state control of key industries.

questions.question: Under which constitutional compromise, known as the 'Munshi-Ayyangar Formula', was Hindi adopted as the official language of the Union alongside a 15-year transition period for English?
options: A) Article 351 of the Indian Constitution
B) Article 348 of the Indian Constitution
C) Article 343 of the Indian Constitution
D) Article 350A of the Indian Constitution
questions.explanation: K.M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar drafted the compromise formula enacted in Article 343, designating Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language while permitting English for 15 years.

questions.question: In the debate on public finance and planning, what was the 'Kaldor Proposal' on Indian tax reform submitted by British economist Nicholas Kaldor in 1956?
options: A) Abolishing all corporate income taxes to attract foreign direct investment from Wall Street
B) Levying a 50% agricultural revenue tax on all small and marginal farmers across dryland regions
C) Funding all Five Year Plans exclusively by printing unbacked currency notes through the Reserve Bank
D) Introducing an integrated direct tax system including an Expenditure Tax, Wealth Tax, and Capital Gains Tax to curb tax evasion by the rich
questions.explanation: Nicholas Kaldor recommended an integrated tax structure comprising income tax, wealth tax, expenditure tax, and capital gains tax to mobilize domestic resources and prevent wealth concentration.

questions.question: Which prominent strategic dialogue initiated in 2007 between India, the United States, Japan, and Australia was revived in 2017 to promote a free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific region?
options: A) Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad)
B) Five Eyes Intelligence Alliance
C) AUKUS Trilateral Pact
D) ANZUS Security Alliance
questions.explanation: First mooted by Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2007, the Quad was revitalized in 2017 as a diplomatic and security consultation among India, the US, Japan, and Australia.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In which state did the Congress split of 1969 cause the regional faction led by Biju Patnaik to break away and form the Utkal Congress?
options: A) West Bengal
B) Odisha
C) Bihar
D) Assam
questions.explanation: In Odisha, veteran leader Biju Patnaik rebelled against the central Congress high command and formed the regional Utkal Congress in 1969, challenging both Congress(O) and Congress(R).

questions.question: What was the significance of the 40th Constitutional Amendment Act enacted during the Emergency in 1976 regarding national maritime boundaries?
options: A) It placed all naval warships under the personal operational command of the Prime Minister's Secretariat
B) It abolished the Indian Coast Guard and merged it into the Central Reserve Police Force
C) It empowered Parliament to determine from time to time the limits of the territorial waters, the continental shelf, the exclusive economic zone (EEZ), and maritime zones of India
D) It declared the Indian Ocean an exclusive sovereign lake of the Republic of India
questions.explanation: The 40th Amendment substituted Article 297, vesting all lands, minerals, and resources within the territorial waters, continental shelf, and EEZ in the Union of India.

questions.question: Which accord signed in December 1988 between the Government of India, the Government of Tripura, and the Tripura National Volunteers (TNV) ended an armed tribal insurgency?
options: A) Shillong Accord
B) Bodo Peace Concordat
C) Karbi Anglong Pact
D) Tripura Peace Accord (signed with TNV leader Bejoy Kumar Hrangkhawl)
questions.explanation: The TNV Accord was signed on 12 August 1988 by Bejoy Hrangkhawl and the central government, leading to the surrender of tribal insurgents and expansion of autonomous district councils.

questions.question: Which theoretical model of coalition government in India, conceptualized by political scientist E. Sridharan, explains how centrist parties act as 'pivotal parties' capable of forming coalitions with either wing?
options: A) Spatial Theory of Coalition Bargaining and Pivotal Parties
B) The Theory of Monolithic Hegemony
C) The Marxist Vanguard Thesis
D) The Feudal Patronage Paradigm
questions.explanation: E. Sridharan analyzed Indian coalitions using spatial party competition, showing how centrist parties (like the Congress or Janata Dal) occupied median ideological positions essential for stable coalition majorities.

questions.question: What was the core principle enunciated by the Supreme Court in the landmark M. Ismail Faruqui v. Union of India (1994) judgment concerning the acquisition of religious places by the state?
options: A) The state cannot acquire any place of worship under any circumstances whatsoever under Article 25
B) A mosque is not an essential part of the practice of the religion of Islam, and religious places of worship can be acquired by the state in the exercise of its sovereign eminent domain
C) Only temples constructed prior to 1857 enjoy absolute constitutional immunity from compulsory acquisition
D) All disputes concerning religious properties must be adjudicated exclusively by a tribunal of religious clerics
questions.explanation: In Ismail Faruqui (1994), upholding the Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Act 1993, the Court ruled that places of worship are acquirable by the state unless the particular place holds unique spiritual significance.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which former Soviet republic was engulfed in a severe frozen conflict in Transnistria, where Russian-speaking separatists broke away following the Soviet collapse in 1992?
options: A) Ukraine
B) Belarus
C) Moldova
D) Lithuania
questions.explanation: Transnistria broke away from Moldova in 1990-1992 with the support of the Russian 14th Guards Army, establishing a de facto unrecognized breakaway state along the Dniester river.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the specialized function of the 'European Stability Mechanism' (ESM) established in 2012 by eurozone member states?
options: A) Purchasing military fighter jets for joint deployment along the Arctic circle
B) Enforcing common criminal penal codes across municipal jurisdictions in Western Europe
C) Managing agricultural foodgrain buffer stocks for the World Food Programme
D) Providing immediate financial assistance and bailouts to eurozone member countries experiencing severe sovereign debt and banking crises
questions.explanation: Created in 2012 in the wake of the European debt crisis, the ESM is a permanent intergovernmental organization in Luxembourg providing emergency financial rescue loans to eurozone states.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Under the 1998 Lahore Declaration signed by Prime Ministers Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif, what critical bilateral commitment was made regarding nuclear risks?
options: A) Notifying each other immediately in the event of accidental, unauthorized or unexplained incident involving nuclear weapons and providing advance notification of ballistic missile tests
B) Surrendering sovereign command of both nuclear arsenals to a joint bilateral military committee
C) Dismantling all nuclear warheads within 30 days under the supervision of the UN Security Council
D) Allowing reciprocal unannounced on-site inspections of all nuclear power reactors by foreign intelligence agents
questions.explanation: The Lahore Declaration (February 1999) committed India and Pakistan to bilateral nuclear confidence-building measures, including advance notification of ballistic missile flight tests.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Under Article 51 of the UN Charter, what inherent right of member states is recognized notwithstanding the Security Council's primary responsibility for peace?
options: A) The right to unilaterally secede from the United Nations General Assembly without financial penalty
B) The inherent right of individual or collective self-defense if an armed attack occurs against a Member of the United Nations
C) The right to deploy nuclear weapons against non-signatories of the UN Charter
D) The right to nationalize foreign embassies situated within their capital cities
questions.explanation: Article 51 explicitly guarantees the inherent right of individual or collective self-defense in the event of an armed attack until the Security Council has taken measures to maintain international peace.

questions.question: Which multilateral export control regime was established in 1987 by the G7 countries to curb the proliferation of unmanned delivery systems capable of delivering weapons of mass destruction?
options: A) Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG)
B) Australia Group
C) Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR)
D) Wassenaar Arrangement
questions.explanation: The MTCR is an informal export control association of 35 nations aimed at preventing the proliferation of missiles and drones capable of carrying a 500 kg payload to a range of at least 300 km (India joined in 2016).

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: What is the core distinction between the 'Kyoto Protocol' (1997) and the 'Paris Agreement' (2015) regarding national emission obligations?
options: A) Kyoto applied only to European nations, while Paris applied exclusively to African and Asian countries
B) Kyoto banned all solar and wind renewable energy technologies, while Paris made coal combustion illegal globally
C) Kyoto was administered by NATO, while Paris is supervised by the World Trade Organization

D) Kyoto imposed top-down legally binding cuts exclusively on developed Annex I nations, while Paris established a bottom-up framework where all countries submit voluntary Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)
questions.explanation: Unlike Kyoto's binary division and top-down targets for developed nations, Paris adopted a universal, bottom-up hybrid model where all nations pledge nationally determined contributions (NDCs) with universal transparency.

questions.question: Which economist authored the influential critique 'Globalization and Its Discontents' (2002), exposing the rigid market fundamentalism and destructive conditionalities of the IMF?
options: A) Joseph E. Stiglitz
B) Paul Krugman
C) Milton Friedman
D) Thomas Piketty
questions.explanation: Nobel laureate and former World Bank chief economist Joseph Stiglitz criticized the IMF for pushing one-size-fits-all austerity, rapid deregulation, and capital market liberalisation on crisis-hit developing nations.

questions.question: Which of the following was a key structural reason why the Socialist Party failed to emerge as an effective national alternative to the Congress during the first three general elections?
options: A) The Socialist Party was legally declared an illegal subversive organisation by the Supreme Court of India

B) The Congress successfully co-opted socialist goals (such as the 1955 Avadi socialistic pattern resolution), leaving socialists ideologically fragmented and continually splitting into rival factions
C) Socialist party leaders were barred from speaking any language other than English in parliamentary debates
D) The Soviet Union sent military funding exclusively to the Swatantra Party to suppress socialist candidates
questions.explanation: The Congress's ideological adaptability, especially adopting a socialistic pattern in 1955, deprived socialists of a distinctive economic platform while internal personal rivalries caused unending party splits.

questions.question: Which constitutional mechanism did the Government of India use to integrate the French settlements of Chandernagore, Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam into the Indian Union?
options: A) A swift military invasion code-named Operation Black Thunder in November 1954
B) A unilateral decree issued by the United Nations Trusteeship Council in New York
C) A bilateral Treaty of Cession signed between the Governments of India and France in May 1956, formally ratified by the French Parliament in August 1962
D) An auction of colonial assets conducted by the International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: Unlike Portugal's resistance in Goa, France negotiated a peaceful transfer: a de facto transfer in November 1954 followed by a formal Treaty of Cession in 1956, ratified in 1962 (14th Constitutional Amendment).

questions.question: What was the administrative controversy surrounding the formulation of the Fourth Five Year Plan, leading to its postponement from 1966 to 1969?
options: A) The complete resignation of all members of the Indian Civil Service across northern India
B) The total refusal of all state governments to accept any federal tax allocations from New Delhi
C) A nationwide referendum in which citizens voted to eliminate all central planning bodies
D) Severe economic dislocation caused by the 1965 war, back-to-back droughts, suspension of foreign aid, and the controversial 36.5% devaluation of the Indian rupee in June 1966
questions.explanation: Economic distress, drought, devaluation of the rupee under US pressure, and inflation paralyzed resource mobilization, compelling the government to adopt three Annual Plans before launching the Fourth Plan in 1969.

questions.question: Which diplomatic event in July 1971 orchestrated by US National Security Advisor Henry Kissinger dramatically shifted the global balance of power and hastened India's treaty with the USSR?
options: A) Kissinger's secret visit to Beijing via Islamabad, laying the groundwork for the US-China strategic rapprochement
B) The signing of a mutual nuclear alliance between the United States and North Vietnam
C) The deployment of American naval fleets to occupy the Malacca Strait
D) The complete expulsion of Taiwan from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund
questions.explanation: Kissinger's secret mission to Beijing via Pakistan revealed a brewing US-China-Pakistan diplomatic axis against India and the USSR, prompting India to sign the Indo-Soviet Treaty of August 1971.

questions.question: In which state did the Railway Strike of May 1974 face the most ruthless government suppression, with striking railway workers evicted from government quarters, dismissed, and arrested under MISA?
options: A) Exclusively in the state of Kerala under the direct supervision of the CPI ministry
B) Across the entire nationwide Indian railway network, with over 30,000 workers arrested in UP, Bihar, West Bengal, and Maharashtra
C) Only in the Union Territory of Goa under a special governor's emergency ordinance
D) Solely in the state of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 emergency regulations
questions.explanation: The 20-day 1974 railway strike was suppressed with unprecedented severity: the government deployed the Territorial Army, BSF, and CRPF, jailed over 30,000 workers, and evicted families from railway colonies.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which of the following Soviet republics held a popular referendum in March 1991 where 70% of citizens voted in favor of preserving the USSR as a renewed federation, yet was swiftly dissolved nine months later?
options: A) The Baltic republics of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania
B) The Caucasian republics of Georgia and Armenia
C) The nine participating republics (including Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, and Central Asian states)
D) The Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic
questions.explanation: In the 17 March 1991 Soviet referendum, 77.8% of voters across nine republics supported preserving the Union; however, subsequent political events (the August coup and republican declarations) overrode the mandate.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which prominent concept was outlined in the 1973 Declaration of European Identity adopted at the Copenhagen Summit of the European Community?
options: A) The mandatory replacement of national languages with a newly invented artificial dialect
B) The formal annexation of all former colonial territories across Africa and Asia
C) The prohibition of any non-European immigrants from residing in Western Europe
D) Defining the shared principles of democracy, rule of law, social justice, and respect for human rights that unite member nations in international relations
questions.explanation: The Copenhagen Summit Declaration on European Identity (1973) defined the dynamic common heritage, values, and democratic identity of Europe to project a unified stance in global affairs.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In Sri Lankan politics, what was the 'Vaddukoddai Resolution' adopted by the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF) in May 1976?
options: A) A peace pact agreeing to dissolve all Tamil political parties in exchange for economic subsidies
B) A historic political resolution calling for the restoration and reconstitution of a free, sovereign, secular, socialist State of Tamil Eelam
C) A constitutional amendment making Sinhala the sole medium of instruction across all northern universities
D) A petition to the British Crown requesting the recolonization of the island of Ceylon
questions.explanation: Adopted under the leadership of S.J.V. Chelvanayakam in 1976, the Vaddukoddai Resolution marked the formal ideological watershed where mainstream Tamil politics demanded a separate sovereign Tamil Eelam.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In global energy geopolitics, what is the strategic importance of the 'Strait of Hormuz' connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman?
options: A) It contains the largest freshwater natural desalination aquifer on the planet
B) It is the designated international deep-sea storage facility for nuclear power plant waste
C) It is an exclusive canal owned and operated by the International Maritime Organization
D) It is the world's most critical maritime petroleum transit choke point, carrying roughly one-fifth of global petroleum liquids consumption
questions.explanation: The Strait of Hormuz is the world's paramount oil transit chokepoint, through which approximately 20-21 million barrels of oil flow daily, making its security vital for global energy markets.
